subject.title: feat: isolate native subagent skill workspaces

question: Should OpenClaw expose a persistent native `sessions_spawn.workspace` mode that intentionally narrows a child session’s skill roots, rather than relying on existing agent-level workspace and skill configuration?
rationale: This is a new user-visible tool capability with persisted session semantics and a least-privilege promise; code review alone cannot determine whether that should become a supported core contract.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow native mode
options.body: Approve an additive native-only `workspace` contract after real isolation proof and explicit documentation of its persistence behavior.

options.title: Keep isolation at agent configuration scope
options.body: Decline the new per-run mode and direct the use case toward existing per-agent workspace and skill configuration.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrow native mode
recommendation.body: Approve an additive native-only `workspace` contract after real isolation proof and explicit documentation of its persistence behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work covers subagent workspace inheritance, spawn metadata, and subagent security boundaries.
